subject: Biology
title: The Living World: Chapter Introduction
summary: A mule cannot reproduce, yet it is alive. Metabolism, cellular organisation and consciousness define life; binomial names and the taxonomic hierarchy organise 1.7-1.8 million described species.
keyPoints: Growth and reproduction are **not defining**: non-living masses grow from outside, and mules do not reproduce.
**Metabolism**, **cellular organisation** and **consciousness** are defining features of life.
About **1.7-1.8 million species** are described: this variety is **biodiversity**.
**Binomial nomenclature** (Linnaeus): genus + species, e.g. *Mangifera indica*, *Homo sapiens*; ranks kingdom → species.

head: Feature
Defining?
Reason
rows: Mountains, boulders and sand mounds also grow, by accumulation from outside
Mules, sterile worker bees and infertile couples do not reproduce
All living organisms carry out chemical reactions; no non-living object does
All life is made of cells
Living organisms sense and respond to their surroundings

blocks.p: The same mango tree has different local names (aam, mango). **Binomial nomenclature**, given by **Carolus Linnaeus**, gives every organism one scientific name of two parts: the **genus** (capital letter) and the **specific epithet** (small letter), printed in italics or underlined when handwritten.

blocks.formula: Kingdom → Phylum/Division → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species

blocks.p: Moving from kingdom to species, organisms share more and more characters.

quiz.q: Which is a defining feature of all living organisms?
quiz.explain: Every living organism carries out metabolism; growth and reproduction have exceptions.

quiz.q: Why is reproduction not a defining feature of life?
options: Mules and worker bees cannot reproduce but are alive

quiz.explain: The first word is the genus.

quiz.q: Which rank is the lowest (most specific)?
quiz.explain: Species is the basic unit of classification.
